findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate DateTime audit-log ordering
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordered field value. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so once any results are returned, cursor construction calls this method with a `datetime` and raises `TypeError` (`datetime` does not implement floor/ceil). Subsequent cursor requests would also pass the integer cursor value directly to a datetime comparison in `build_queryset`. As a result, an authorized caller using `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 instead of audit-log results. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible key serialization and cursor deserialization, or the endpoint must use a paginator that supports datetime keys.

findings.title: Advanced negative offsets cause Django QuerySet slicing errors
findings.body: The advanced branch deliberately passes a negative `start_offset` to a Django `QuerySet` slice, but Django does not support negative indexing/slicing for querysets and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The cursor parser accepts signed integer offsets, so an administrator can trigger this path with an `optimized_pagination=true` request containing a cursor with a negative offset, producing a 500. Negative offsets must be rejected or translated into a supported query; they cannot be used as Python-style reverse indexes on querysets.
